findings.title: Shoppers cannot purchase groceries in the supplied configuration — Razorpay credentials are absent
findings.surface: /cart Pay with Razorpay; POST /api/orders/checkout
findings.observed: Third-party integrations / Payments and billing: with the supplied environment and no external process override, every shopper reaching Pay receives 'Online payments are not configured yet' and no order can be placed. The user explicitly disallows offline payment, so there is no supported purchasing alternative. This is a source prediction; runtime-injected nonempty Razorpay credentials would change the configuration conclusion. The safe 503 itself meets R-013.
findings.evidence: backend/.env:1-7 supplies database, CORS and Clerk configuration but no Razorpay credentials. backend/routes_orders.py:44 reads only RAZORPAY_KEY_ID and RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET; :45-46 raises 503 if either is absent; :72 calls this before creating an order. frontend/src/pages/Checkout.jsx:77 initiates that route.
findings.expected: request: "Razorpay" and "only prepayment"; R-012: "The checkout payment step creates its charge through Razorpay"; checklist, Third-party integrations: "When every configuration source the code reads leaves a required provider value empty or a placeholder, file the blocked feature". A shopper must be able to pay online and place an order.
reproduction_steps: With the supplied environment and no externally injected Razorpay credentials, sign in as a customer.
Add a product, open Checkout and enter a valid delivery address.
Press Pay with Razorpay; the API rejects checkout with 503 instead of opening a payable order.

findings.title: Two shoppers can both pay for the last unit — stock is checked before payment but decremented without a reservation or stock guard
findings.surface: POST /api/orders/checkout; POST /api/orders/{id}/verify
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations / Data, persistence and APIs: when configured payments are available and product stock is 1, two customers can each check out qty 1 before either pays. Both confirmations become paid placed orders, while only one unit exists; clamping stock to zero conceals rather than prevents the shortage. One prepaid customer cannot receive the purchased goods and needs manual cancellation/refund. The same flaw allows a single customer to pay an old pending order after stock sells out.
findings.evidence: backend/routes_orders.py:63 checks p['stock'] during checkout; :87-94 writes pending_payment without reserving inventory; :116-120 marks the order paid; :123 decrements stock by id alone, then :124 clamps negatives to zero.
findings.expected: R-038: "Two submissions arriving together must not both pass the stock check for the same last unit"; R-058: "A paid order decrements each product's stock exactly once by its ordered quantity"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "competing reservations must respect capacity". With stock S=1, total committed quantity cannot exceed 1.
reproduction_steps: With working Razorpay configuration, set a product's stock to 1.
Have two customers start separate checkouts for one unit before either completes payment.
Complete both payments and verification.
Both orders are placed and paid although only one unit can be fulfilled.

findings.title: A paid shopper can lose their order after a callback interruption — payment completion exists only in the browser verify handler
findings.surface: Razorpay checkout completion; /orders
findings.observed: Payments and billing / UI state, navigation and interaction: if payment succeeds but the tab closes, connectivity fails before verify reaches the backend, or its request fails, the charge has happened yet the order remains pending_payment, invisible in My Orders and unavailable to fulfillment. There is no server webhook, status reconciliation, or customer retry-payment/verify control. Retrying Pay starts a new provider order rather than recovering the paid one, risking another charge. Recovery requires operator/provider intervention.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/Checkout.jsx:83-85 calls verify solely in Razorpay's browser handler; :89-90 only toasts a failed verify. backend/routes_orders.py:100-125 is the only payment confirmation path; :130 filters history to payment.status='paid'. server.py:29-33 includes routers with no Razorpay webhook/reconciliation route; checkout stores pending at routes_orders.py:91-92.
findings.expected: R-084: "After a successful payment ... the order appears in /orders"; checklist, Payments and billing: "paid state follows a verified webhook or server status check"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "a send timing out after delivery must reconcile before retrying". A captured payment must eventually yield one recoverable, visible order even if the browser is interrupted.
reproduction_steps: With working payment configuration, start checkout and complete payment.
Interrupt the browser/network before POST /orders/{id}/verify reaches the server, or encounter a verification request failure.
Reload and open My Orders.
The charged order is omitted; the checkout offers only a new payment rather than recovery.

findings.title: Concurrent cancellation restores stock twice or a rider can resurrect a cancelled delivery — transition writes ignore the checked state
findings.surface: Admin Cancel; rider delivery status; order assignment/status APIs
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations / Data, persistence and APIs: two admin tabs cancelling the same placed order can both read placed, both write cancelled and both increment stock, manufacturing saleable inventory. Separately, a rider can read assigned, then an admin cancels/restocks, then the rider's delayed update changes cancelled to out_for_delivery. Paid terminal outcomes and stock no longer agree; the user may be promised/delivered cancelled goods or later buy nonexistent stock. Sequential replay is guarded, but these reachable concurrent requests are not.
findings.evidence: routes_admin.py:112-114 reads/checks state, then :116 updates by {'id': order_id} only; :118-120 independently returns inventory for each request. routes_orders.py:183-187 checks assignment/state before :189 updates by id alone. routes_admin.py:105 assignment also writes by id alone. frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminOrders.jsx:77-87 has no pending-action guard.
findings.expected: R-052: "returns each line's quantity ... exactly once"; R-053: "a step taken out of order ... is refused"; R-049: "not assigned to them ... status and timeline are unchanged"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "conditional/atomic operations ... compensation" must preserve transition invariants.
reproduction_steps: Open the same paid placed order in two admin sessions.
Confirm Cancel in both before either request finishes; both can restore the same stock.
Alternatively, have a rider start delivery while an admin cancels the assigned order.
If the cancellation commits between the rider read and write, the rider overwrites cancelled with out_for_delivery.

findings.title: A paid order can permanently leave inventory unchanged after an interruption — payment commits before non-recoverable stock writes
findings.surface: POST /api/orders/{id}/verify inventory commit
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs / Payments and billing: if a database error or worker interruption occurs after the paid update but before all inventory writes, the paid order persists with no or partial stock decrement. A retry returns success through the paid short-circuit and never repairs the missing adjustment. The admin may fulfill that order while the shop resells the still-listed stock, causing consequential prepaid shortages. This is a conditional source prediction for that failure boundary.
findings.evidence: routes_orders.py:116-120 first commits payment.status='paid'; :121-124 then adjusts each product in separate writes. :106-107 immediately returns on any future verify if payment is already paid; no transaction, effect marker or reconciliation job exists.
findings.expected: R-058: "A paid order decrements each product's stock exactly once"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure". Retrying after an interrupted inventory update must finish remaining adjustments, not skip them.
reproduction_steps: With configured payments, pay for an order containing two distinct products.
Encounter worker interruption or database write failure after order payment commit but before the second inventory update.
Retry the verify request or reopen the order.
The order is paid, but the missing stock effect is permanently skipped.

findings.title: Two simultaneous role changes can lock the store out of its admin console — last-admin protection is a read-then-write race
findings.surface: /admin/users role selector; PATCH /api/users/{user_id}/role
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control / Data, persistence and APIs: with exactly two admins, concurrent demotion requests can each count two and both set their targets to customer. The store is then left with no account able to approve riders, manage catalogue or fulfill orders; signing back in does not restore an existing customer's role. Recovery requires out-of-app operator intervention. Scope is the reachable two-admin interleaving, not every role change.
findings.evidence: routes_admin.py:264-266 counts current admins before :267 updates only {'user_id': user_id}; no transaction/shared guard serializes two demotions. AdminUsers.jsx:25-30 permits role updates from multiple sessions. current_member (core.py:110-112) only bootstraps an admin for new/roleless members, not already demoted ones.
findings.expected: R-050: "demoting the last remaining admin is refused so at least one admin always exists"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Walk plausible interleavings ... conditional/atomic operations". After any two valid administrative changes at least one admin must remain.
reproduction_steps: Have exactly two admin accounts, A and B.
From their concurrent admin sessions demote A and B to Customer before either update commits.
Both requests can pass count_documents==2.
Both accounts now receive 403 on admin operations, with no remaining administrator.

findings.title: Editing a price can put an already sold unit back on sale — product saves overwrite live stock with the dialog's stale snapshot
findings.surface: /admin/products Edit product; PUT /api/admin/products/{id}
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs / Business logic and calculations: admin opens Edit product at stock 1, then a shopper pays for its final unit (stored stock becomes 0). Admin changes only price and saves; the old stock=1 is sent and overwrites 0. The storefront sells that unit again even though it was already committed to a paid order. Reloading the form before saving is not a reliable or indicated concurrency safeguard; shortages require manual correction/refund.
findings.evidence: ProductDialog.jsx:33 snapshots stock when the dialog opens and :46-47 submits it on every save, even a price-only edit. routes_admin.py:167-169 unconditionally $sets the whole submitted ProductIn, including stock. Payment verification separately decrements current stock (routes_orders.py:123), without any shared product version.
findings.expected: R-058: "A paid order decrements each product's stock exactly once by its ordered quantity"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: prevent "lost/overwritten valid work" across concurrent operations. A price edit must not undo a sale that occurred after the form was opened.
reproduction_steps: Open Edit product for an item with stock 1.
Before saving, let a shopper pay for one unit and finish verification.
Change only Selling price in the still-open dialog and Save product.
Stock is reset to the stale value 1 and the sold unit becomes purchasable again.

findings.title: A late invalid confirmation can hide a paid order and cause a second stock deduction — failure handling overwrites paid state unconditionally
findings.surface: POST /api/orders/{id}/verify concurrent valid/invalid confirmations
findings.observed: Payments and billing / Data, persistence and APIs: an invalid verify request can read pending, pause, then overwrite failed after a valid verify has paid the same order and decremented stock. The paid shopper's order vanishes from history/fulfillment queries. Replaying the real valid confirmation then sees failed and decrements stock again. This requires concurrent requests for the same owner's order; it does not expose another user's order or permit forged payment success.
findings.evidence: routes_orders.py:106 reads an unpaid status once; :112-113 handles invalid signatures by updating {'id': order_id} to payment.status='failed' without a status predicate. A concurrent valid request uses :116-120 to mark paid and :123 decrements inventory. The paid short circuit only applies at the earlier read.
findings.expected: R-055: "a bad Razorpay signature fails and leaves the order unpaid, while a valid signature marks it paid once"; R-058: replay does not decrement stock again; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions". Invalid confirmation must not overwrite a concurrently committed valid payment.
reproduction_steps: For an unpaid order, submit an invalid signature verification and a real valid provider confirmation concurrently.
Let both read pending; let valid confirmation commit first, then invalid-signature failure update commit.
The order is now payment failed despite the valid payment and inventory decrement.
Replay the valid confirmation: it can mark paid and decrement inventory a second time.

findings.title: Signed-out sessions retain API access until token expiry — backend verifies JWTs but never checks revocation
findings.surface: GET /api/me and every authenticated API
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: a previously obtained valid bearer token continues to read the owner's profile/orders or act with their role after Clerk sign-out, until its JWT expiry. This creates a bounded stale-access window for a copied token; expiry still applies, and the code does not establish indefinite access. The app cannot enforce the promised next-request logout rejection.
findings.evidence: clerk_auth.py:115-116 verifies a signature and decodes expiration; :130-131 returns claims['sub'] and session_id without consulting Clerk session status. core.py:107-121 trusts require_user and reads the local member; there is no session revocation lookup.
findings.expected: R-034: "A Clerk session token invalidated by sign-out is refused ... with 401"; checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: "next-request rejection of revoked/deleted sessions". Revoked sessions must no longer authorize protected data access.
reproduction_steps: Sign in and retain the session's current bearer token.
Sign out through Clerk.
Before the token expires, request /api/me with that token.
The backend still accepts its signature and returns user data rather than checking the signed-out session.

findings.title: Returning shoppers see obsolete cart prices and stock — restored snapshots are never refreshed in the shared cart
findings.surface: Header cart total, My basket sheet and mobile cart bar after reload
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: add a ₹50 item, let an admin change its price to ₹60 and stock to 0, then reload the storefront. The sheet/header still quote ₹50 and allow increases using old stock. Only /cart independently substitutes current data, so the shopper sees contradictory bills/availability and must rework the basket. Backend pricing prevents charging the obsolete price; the defect is bounded presentation and cart-state impairment.
findings.evidence: CartContext.jsx:9 loads entire localStorage snapshots; :30 saves price and stock; :43-45 totals those snapshots without a product fetch. CartSheet.jsx:37-52 renders those values. Checkout.jsx:25-32 fetches live products only in its own local hook, never updating CartContext.
findings.expected: R-036: "The restored cart's prices and stock come from GET /api/products at page load"; R-005: "displayed total must equal ... backend". The shared restored cart should quote current ₹60 and current availability everywhere.
reproduction_steps: Add a product priced ₹50 with available stock.
As admin change its price to ₹60 and stock to zero.
Reload the shop and open My basket.
Observe old price/stock there, then open Checkout to see different live values.

findings.title: Shoppers and staff mistake failed loads for empty data or lost access — fetch errors are converted to empty or null results
findings.surface: /shop, /orders, /delivery, admin tables, protected role lookup and product detail
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: a network outage, 401/403, or server failure reads as genuine zero products/orders/users/applications for shoppers and staff rather than a failed fetch. A rider can believe they have no jobs; customers cannot distinguish missing purchases from an unavailable API. If only the related rail fails, an otherwise usable product is hidden as unavailable. A failed role lookup tells legitimate staff they lack access. Reload is a possible recovery but no error explains it.
findings.evidence: Shop.jsx:42 catches into setProducts([]), then :80-84 says 'No items found'. Orders.jsx:15 catches into setOrders([]), then :26 says 'No orders yet'. AdminOrders.jsx:66, DeliveryDashboard.jsx:54, AdminRiders.jsx:22, AdminProducts.jsx:21 and AdminUsers.jsx:18 similarly substitute empty data. ProductDetail.jsx:20-23 treats even a failed related-products fetch as setMissing(true), hiding an already loaded product. MeContext.jsx:23-24 discards a failed /me fetch as null with no error state, so RoleGate.jsx:25 reports no access.
findings.expected: R-030: "Every failed action ... shows a plain-language message naming what went wrong and what to do next"; R-068: "a failed fetch shows an error rather than an empty table". Keep real empty/no-access states separate from request failure and offer retry.
reproduction_steps: Open Shop, My orders, My deliveries or an admin table while its API request fails.
The UI displays its normal zero-results state or blank table rather than a fetch error.
On a product page, let the detail request succeed but the subsequent related-products request fail; the whole detail is replaced with unavailable.
Let /me fail for an admin opening /admin: after loading, the guard presents no access instead of the failed identity lookup.

findings.title: Products and older orders become unreachable as the store grows — list APIs silently truncate without pagination
findings.surface: GET /api/products, /shop; /api/admin/orders; /orders; /delivery
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs / Performance and resource leaks: with 201 active matching products a shopper can never browse the last product; repeated smaller-limit requests always return the same prefix. At 301 paid orders, admins lose access to older orders' assignment/cancellation controls from the list; customer/rider history and totals similarly become incomplete at their caps. Specific known product IDs can still be opened, but omitted IDs are not discoverable via paging. No runtime timing claim is made.
findings.evidence: routes_store.py:42 only accepts limit (max 200), :52 returns a capped bare list with no cursor/offset/count. Shop.jsx:41 requests limit 200 with no next-page control. routes_admin.py:83 limits orders to 300; routes_orders.py:131 limits customer history to 100, :178 rider orders to 200, each without paging. DeliveryDashboard.jsx:84 calls a count derived from this slice 'All delivered'.
findings.expected: R-076: "every matching product exactly once across its pages"; R-088: "by paging rather than returning everything"; R-099: lists the customer's own orders; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "pagination reaches the last page ... exposes truncation". All records must remain reachable, with counts for the same population.
reproduction_steps: Grow the active catalogue to 201 products and open All groceries.
Only 200 appear and there is no next page.
Repeat GET /api/products with limit=10 and attempted later page parameters: the same first ten return.
With more than 300 paid orders or 100 customer orders, inspect the corresponding history and try to reach the omitted oldest rows.

findings.title: Customers tracking an open order never see delivery progress — order detail fetches only on mount
findings.surface: /orders/:id status and timeline
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: a customer leaves their placed order open while a rider marks it out for delivery and delivered. Its badge, timeline and rider information remain at the initial state indefinitely. Manual browser reload recovers the data, but nothing on this tracking screen signals that it is stale or lets the customer refresh it.
findings.evidence: OrderDetail.jsx:42-44 fetches only when api or id changes; :58 renders status and :60 renders timeline from that one stored response. There is no poll, subscription, visibility refresh or refresh control. Rider updates persist via routes_orders.py:189-190 but no consumer event updates the customer's page.
findings.expected: R-054: "it updates after the rider marks the order delivered"; users rely on: "Track my order" (Footer.jsx:33) exposing current delivery progress. The open tracking page should refresh persisted changes or provide an explicit refresh action.
reproduction_steps: Open a customer's order detail while it is assigned.
In the rider dashboard advance it to out for delivery and delivered.
Return to the still-open customer page; the original badge and timeline remain until a full browser reload.

findings.title: Neither AI surface can answer with the supplied configuration — model key is absent and direct environment lookup raises an unhandled error
findings.surface: Ask AI; Generate insights; POST /api/ai/chat and /api/admin/ai/insights
findings.observed: Third-party integrations / AI and model features: absent an externally injected model key, both requested AI features raise KeyError before calling the provider. The supplied environment cannot generate shopping replies or sales insights, and the missing-key error is an unhandled 500 rather than a deliberate configuration message. Other shopping/admin work remains possible. A nonempty process-level EMERGENT_LLM_KEY override would remove this configuration blocker; provider/model acceptance has not been executed.
findings.evidence: routes_ai.py:26 indexes os.environ['EMERGENT_LLM_KEY'] directly. Neither backend/.env:1-7 nor frontend/.env:1-3 supplies it. :97 and :135 construct the chat before entering _stream's try/except (:32-42). server.py has no exception handler for this failure. streamSSE (frontend/src/lib/api.js:27-33) consequently displays a generic failure.
findings.expected: R-018: "call ... with the injected key ... a missing key ... comes back as an error the screen can show"; checklist, Third-party integrations: report required provider values absent from all read config sources. Shoppers and admins should receive real AI results when configured and a deliberate readable unconfigured response otherwise.
reproduction_steps: Run with supplied configuration and no externally injected model key.
Sign in and send a question to Ask AI.
As admin press Generate insights.
Both endpoints fail during client construction instead of streaming a reply or returning a readable configuration error.

findings.title: Clearing an active AI reply can crash the chat and resurrect erased text — clear neither cancels nor versions the pending stream
findings.surface: Ask AI → Clear chat during streaming
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction / AI and model features: with a configured provider, clear a conversation after its first streamed text but before completion. The next delta tries to read content from an undefined last message inside a React state updater, predicting a render error with no app error boundary. Even if no further delta arrives, the server's on_done reinserts the assistant reply after the clear, so it returns on reload. Users lose a usable chat surface and cannot reliably erase an in-flight reply without waiting/reloading.
findings.evidence: ChatBody.jsx:108 leaves Clear chat enabled during busy; :87-88 deletes history then setsMessages([]). :76 subsequently calls patchLast; :65 invokes fn(c[c.length-1]) even if the list is empty, and :76 dereferences l.content. routes_ai.py:101-103 saves the still-running assistant response without a clear/version check after :117 deletes messages.
findings.expected: R-016: "a clear request empties only that user's history"; R-087: one active stream without duplicated messages; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions". Clearing an active conversation must safely cancel or ignore its pending reply and leave history empty.
reproduction_steps: Send a question to Ask AI with a working provider.
While the reply is streaming, press Clear chat.
Let another delta arrive, or let generation complete, then reload chat.
The next delta targets a nonexistent bubble; the server can also repopulate cleared history with the orphaned reply.

findings.title: Reopening chat permits overlapping replies and extra provider work — closing the panel never releases its stream
findings.surface: Ask AI open/close while generating; streamSSE
findings.observed: Performance and resource leaks / AI and model features: start a long reply, close and reopen chat, then send another question. The old stream remains owned by an unmounted component while a second stream starts, incurring overlapping provider work and independently appending responses into the same history. Late replies can appear out of conversational order on reload. This is bounded by reply duration/provider behavior, not a measured indefinite leak.
findings.evidence: AssistantWidget.jsx:43-44 conditionally mounts Panel; ChatBody.jsx:75 starts streamSSE with no cleanup effect. api.js:22 fetch has no AbortSignal and :35-48 holds the reader until EOF. Closing removes ChatBody and its busy state, so reopening mounts a fresh idle instance while the previous fetch continues; both server requests save replies through routes_ai.py:101-103.
findings.expected: R-087: "Opening and closing ... keeps one active stream at a time"; checklist, Performance and resource leaks: "polling ends with its owner" and subscriptions/streams release on interrupted work. Reopening must resume or cancel the existing operation before starting another.
reproduction_steps: Send a question and close the assistant before it finishes.
Immediately reopen Ask AI and send another question.
Both requests remain active because neither close nor unmount aborts the first.
Reload history after both complete to see independently interleaved replies.

findings.title: Fast filter changes can show the wrong catalogue under the selected category — old fetch responses overwrite newer results
findings.surface: /shop category/search/sort; admin order filters; product navigation
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: select Fruits then Dairy while requests are delayed; if the old Fruits response completes last, the URL/title/category show Dairy but product rows show Fruits indefinitely. Switching sort/search and admin order filters has the same response-order problem. A reload can recover; until then users browse/act on rows under the wrong filter and counts.
findings.evidence: Shop.jsx:39-43 starts a request on each category/q/sort change and every response unconditionally setsProducts; no cleanup/generation comparison exists. :50 and :64 derive the heading from current URL params regardless of which request populated rows. ProductDetail.jsx:20-23 and AdminOrders.jsx:65-71 likewise apply stale responses unconditionally.
findings.expected: R-001: category tiles "open the matching filtered listing"; R-067: URL restores "the same filtered, sorted list"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: destination/object/content must match the initiating reference. The latest filter must own its displayed result.
reproduction_steps: Open Shop and select Fruits & Vegetables.
Before its fetch completes, select Dairy & Bakery.
Let Dairy's response arrive first and Fruits' delayed response arrive second.
The selected category and URL say Dairy but the rows are the older Fruits result.

findings.title: A rejected applicant can retain delivery access after competing reviews — approval and rejection do not atomically claim pending status
findings.surface: /admin/partners Approve/Reject; application review APIs
findings.observed: Auth, sessions and access control / Data, persistence and APIs: two admins can both read pending, one approves (granting delivery), and the other commits rejection afterward. The application then says rejected with a note while the account remains delivery and can receive customer addresses/orders. A write failure between approval's two writes can similarly leave a delivery role on a pending application. This contradicts the rejection decision and requires manual role correction.
findings.evidence: _pending_application reads status at :198-202; approve then writes the role at :215 and application at :216 separately. Reject also reads pending at :222 before writing by id alone at :223-224. Neither write predicates on the previously checked pending state. AdminRiders.jsx:66-67 leaves both review actions available without a busy guard.
findings.expected: R-024: "rejecting keeps the role customer and stores the admin's note"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "stale work must respect later decisions"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Multi-document operations leave no half-written state on failure". One authoritative review must determine both application and role.
reproduction_steps: Open the same pending application in two admin sessions.
Approve it in A while B's rejection has already passed its pending read.
Let B's rejection write finish after A's approval.
GET /me reports role delivery alongside a rejected application; the rider dashboard remains authorized.

findings.title: Different customers can receive the same order reference — short random numbers lack a uniqueness constraint
findings.surface: Checkout-generated public order numbers; admin order-number search
findings.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: two UUIDs with the same eight-character prefix produce the same public MB order reference and both inserts succeed because their full internal ids differ. The namespace is 16^8=4,294,967,296; collisions become appreciable as the store grows (birthday collision probability is about one-half around 77,000 numbers). Admin search and support/customer references become ambiguous. Internal ID-based fulfillment still distinguishes the orders, so this is recoverable reference impairment rather than duplicate charging.
findings.evidence: routes_orders.py:76 constructs order_number as 'MB' plus only the first eight hex characters of a fresh UUID. core.py:47-52 indexes id uniquely but has no order_number unique index or retry on collision. AdminOrders.jsx:114 displays/searches the order by this number; routes_admin.py:82 filters order_number.
findings.expected: R-075: "Every order receives a distinct order_number ... a unique value enforced by the store"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "store-enforced uniqueness". Distinct logical orders must not share their public reference.
reproduction_steps: Create two orders whose generated number UUIDs share the same first eight hex characters.
Both inserts succeed with different internal ids and identical order_number.
Search that order number in Admin Orders; two different customer orders have the same public reference.

findings.title: Empty or interrupted AI output is presented as a finished answer — neither stream endpoint nor consumer validates completion
findings.surface: AI SSE backend and shared client; Ask AI reply completion
findings.observed: AI and model features / UI state, navigation and interaction: if the provider completes with no text, the backend saves an empty assistant message and declares done; chat re-enables sending while its bubble spins forever. If the network stream ends cleanly before the done frame, the client likewise presents partial text as completed without warning. There is no completion/nonempty validation or retry status. These are conditional provider/transport boundary predictions, not observed model outputs.
findings.evidence: routes_ai.py:33-38 stops iteration at StreamDone or iterator exhaustion, then :43-45 saves joined parts and emits done even when no TextDelta arrived. api.js:39-40 treats EOF as success without requiring a done event; ChatBody.jsx:75-78 never tracks done and :30 displays an endless loader for empty content.
findings.expected: R-018: errors "never an empty string or a canned reply"; R-078: "ends with the full text"; R-081: "never an empty bubble"; checklist, AI and model features: validate "empty/malformed results, ... interruption" before final presentation/persistence.
reproduction_steps: With a configured AI provider, send a shopping question.
Encounter a provider stream that ends or emits StreamDone without TextDelta text.
The app persists an empty assistant turn and leaves a spinner bubble rather than an error.
Alternatively, encounter HTTP stream EOF after some deltas but before done; the partial answer appears finished.

findings.title: Sending before history loads can corrupt or crash chat — late history hydration replaces the active reply
findings.surface: Ask AI initial history loading and suggestion buttons
findings.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction / AI and model features: open chat and immediately send a suggestion while history is still fetching. A delayed empty-history response removes the new pair; the next delta reads undefined.content and predicts a React render failure. With existing history it instead appends the new answer onto the previous historical message. Reopening/reloading can recover persisted turns, but the active conversation is lost or corrupted.
findings.evidence: ChatBody.jsx:48 unconditionally replaces messages with history when its request completes; :40 initializes an empty list with immediately usable suggestions/input (:94-113). send at :71 appends a new user/assistant pair before history is loaded; :65 and :76 then append deltas to whichever last message the history response installed.
findings.expected: R-015: opening chat "streams a reply ... conversation is still there after a reload"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "initial, ... pending ... state" and stale work must preserve the current operation. History hydration must not overwrite a new in-flight turn.
reproduction_steps: Open Ask AI with a delayed /ai/chat/history request.
Immediately click a suggested question.
Let history return after send has appended its blank assistant bubble but before the next streamed delta.
The history response replaces that bubble; subsequent deltas target the wrong or absent last message.

findings.title: Indian shoppers' early-morning orders appear on the previous reporting day — daily aggregates use UTC without labelling a different store timezone
findings.surface: Admin Orders today and 7-day chart; rider Delivered today; AI sales data
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations: during 00:00–05:29 IST, new orders/deliveries count under the previous UTC day; Orders today can include yesterday evening's work and the seven-day chart allocates Indian early-morning sales to the prior labelled day. Rider Delivered today likewise uses UTC instead of the rider/store day. Lifetime revenue is unaffected; admins/riders get misleading daily reports and AI inherits the same daily figures.
findings.evidence: compute_stats uses datetime.now(timezone.utc) (:17), groups dates by the UTC timestamp prefix (:26), and starts today at UTC date (:39). DeliveryDashboard.jsx:75 defines today via new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10), and :84 compares stored UTC prefixes. Normal order displays use local toLocaleString in lib/format.js:7.
findings.expected: R-060: "Dates follow the store's day boundary"; checklist, Business logic and calculations: "date/time semantics ... user's zone ... time-window boundaries". Inferred from the Indian-store benchmark and en-IN UI, a store day is Asia/Kolkata unless another timezone is explicitly labelled. Jan 2 00:15 IST equals Jan 1 18:45 UTC and belongs to Jan 2, not Jan 1.
reproduction_steps: Use the store in India shortly after midnight, e.g. Jan 2 at 00:15 IST.
Place/pay an order and mark a delivery complete.
Inspect Orders today, the dated revenue chart and Delivered today.
The implementation derives Jan 1 from the UTC timestamps rather than Jan 2's Indian calendar day.

findings.title: AI chat leaves keyboard focus behind its fullscreen overlay and can hide its close control — panel bypasses dialog focus and viewport constraints
findings.surface: Ask AI panel, mobile keyboard use and short desktop/tablet windows
findings.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: on mobile, opening chat removes its focused opener but never moves focus into the fullscreen panel; Tab traverses the underlying header/page controls concealed by it, and Escape does not close it. At a supported desktop/tablet width with a short 500px viewport, its 600px height plus 24px bottom offset puts its top at -124px, hiding the title and close control. These are source-derived focus/geometry predictions, not measured browser results. Closing by other input or resizing is recoverable, but keyboard/short-window chat use is materially impaired.
findings.evidence: AssistantWidget.jsx:20-21 renders a plain fixed div covering inset-0 on mobile, with no dialog role/aria-modal, focus scope or Escape handler; :30 is the only close action. Unlike cart/admin dialogs, it does not use the Radix dialog primitives. At md it fixes height to 600px with bottom 24px and no max-height.
findings.expected: checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "keyboard focus ... follows the active surface" and an overlay preserves "focus/background interaction contract"; "primary content and controls visible". An active fullscreen assistant must move/contain focus and remain closable within the viewport.
reproduction_steps: On a phone-sized screen, open Ask AI using the keyboard and press Tab.
Focus can move through the obscured page rather than into a modal focus scope; press Escape and the panel stays open.
At width at least 768px and height 500px, open Ask AI.
The fixed 600px panel begins above the viewport, including its close control.

findings.title: Riders can deliver orders that never passed packing — assignment permits placed orders and tracking fabricates completion of skipped steps
findings.surface: Admin Orders Assign rider; rider delivery progression; customer timeline
findings.observed: Business logic and calculations / UI state, navigation and interaction: an admin assigns a newly placed paid order without marking packed; the rider can immediately start and finish delivery. The customer's timeline paints Packed as completed although it was never recorded. This can dispatch work before goods are prepared and misstates progress; staff can safely recover by ensuring packing manually, but the promised lifecycle is not enforced.
findings.evidence: AdminOrders.jsx:92 says 'Assign a rider once packed', but :17 enables assignment for placed orders. routes_admin.py:96 permits placed and :105 changes it directly to assigned; rider NEXT (routes_orders.py:156) allows assigned→out_for_delivery. OrderStatus.jsx:13,18 sets every earlier FLOW step done, including packed, regardless of actual timeline entries.
findings.expected: R-053: "An order moves placed, packed, out_for_delivery, delivered ... a step taken out of order ... is refused"; exposed UI promise (AdminOrders.jsx:92): "Assign a rider once packed". Fulfillment must not skip the packing prerequisite or display it as completed without that step.
reproduction_steps: Open a newly placed order in Admin Orders without pressing Mark packed.
Select a rider from Assign rider.
As that rider press Picked up — start delivery, then Mark as delivered.
The order completes without any packed timeline event while customer tracking paints packing complete.

findings_minor.title: Customers cannot see when their order progressed — timeline hides mobile times and discards stored history entries
findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: customers viewing a delivered order at 375px see no timestamps; desktop sees a date fragment rather than the time of each step. Cancelled orders hide all their actual history, and repeated assignment entries collapse to the last one. Status is still visible and order history is safely retained server-side, so the loss is a minor tracking-detail omission recoverable only outside this UI.
findings_minor.evidence: OrderStatus.jsx:11 replaces cancelled timelines entirely with a note. :14 collapses timeline entries to one value per status with Object.fromEntries. :29 renders timestamps only at sm and above ('hidden sm:block') and strips fmtDate to split(',').slice(0,1), removing the clock portion produced by format.js:7.
findings_minor.expected: R-054: "every timeline entry with its time"; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: preserve the referenced record's content. Tracking should expose when actual transitions occurred, including cancellation, on the rider/customer phone-sized surface.
reproduction_steps: Open an order with placed, assigned, out-for-delivery and delivered timeline timestamps on a phone.
No times appear.
Open the same order on desktop; only date fragments appear.
Open a cancelled order; all timeline entries are replaced by the refund note.

findings_minor.title: Products with missing images show broken media — image consumers have no fallback placeholder
findings_minor.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX / Files, media and generated artifacts: an admin can save an HTTPS image URL returning 404. Catalogue cards and detail retain their dimensions but show a browser-broken image/alt text rather than the promised product placeholder. Product labels and shopping controls remain usable; this is minor presentation degradation, not a purchasing barrier.
findings_minor.evidence: ProductCard.jsx:8-9 and ProductDetail.jsx:40 render bare img elements with no onError/fallback; global styles and App.css add no image-error placeholder. ProductDialog.jsx:22 accepts syntactically valid URLs without checking that an image exists, as appropriate, so an unavailable image is a supported saved value.
findings_minor.expected: R-065: "A product whose image URL is broken or empty renders a placeholder at the same size"; checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: serving accepted content must have a usable consumer outcome. A failed image should have an explicit fallback, not a broken-image rendering.
reproduction_steps: As admin save a product image URL pointing to a missing image.
Open its listing and product detail.
The bare img fails without replacement; no placeholder is rendered.

findings_minor.title: Pending riders are told their access may be a mistake — delivery guard omits their known application status
findings_minor.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: a pending applicant opening /delivery gets only 'You don't have access ... Contact the store admin if ... mistake', not their actual under-review state. Authorization is safe and /partner still shows pending, so this is a small avoidable navigation/status confusion rather than access leakage.
findings_minor.evidence: App.js:41 routes /delivery through RoleGate roles=['delivery']; RoleGate.jsx:25 returns a generic NoAccess when the customer role is not included. NoAccess (:12-17) never reads me.application or links to /partner. Partner.jsx:93 has an under-review status, but this route never reaches it.
findings_minor.expected: R-070: "A customer whose delivery application is still pending ... is shown their application status instead of the dashboard". Keep delivery access blocked while explaining the actual pending review and how to return to it.
reproduction_steps: Submit a delivery partner application as a customer.
Before approval, navigate directly to /delivery.
The page says no access and suggests contacting admin instead of explaining the pending application.

findings_minor.title: Admins undercount low-stock items beyond 50 — KPI counts a capped query rather than all eligible products
findings_minor.surface: Admin overview Low stock items KPI, panel and AI input
findings_minor.observed: Business logic and calculations / Data, persistence and APIs: once 51 active products have stock under 10, the KPI incorrectly reports 50 and AI insights receive that capped count. The panel also omits rows without saying it is a preview. Manage still opens the catalogue with actual stocks, so admins can recover by inspecting it; this is a minor summary/count defect rather than lost inventory.
findings_minor.evidence: routes_admin.py:30-31 reads at most 50 low-stock products with to_list(50); :46 sets low_stock_count=len(low_stock) and returns only low_stock[:8]. AdminOverview.jsx:18 labels that count 'Low stock items' without a cap qualifier; :75 renders the eight-row subset.
findings_minor.expected: R-061: low stock lists products meeting the threshold with current stock; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "count/total ... labels" match the population they summarize and "exposes truncation". If 51 products have stock below 10, the Low stock items count is 51.
reproduction_steps: Have 51 active catalogue products each at stock 9.
Open Store overview.
Low stock items displays 50 and the panel shows only eight rows without a preview count.

findings_minor.title: Customers find no usable advertised support contact — template company details and app identity were left in the shipped shell
findings_minor.surface: Storefront footer Company contact and browser metadata
findings_minor.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: all storefront customers see placeholder company/support details and the generic template browser title. In particular a shopper looking for help with an order cannot use the advertised Support text to contact anyone. Shopping controls remain usable, so the evidenced harm is minor incomplete product-shell content, not a claim that an unpromised support-ticket system is required.
findings_minor.evidence: Footer.jsx:34 renders 'Support: [support email]' and :35 'Store address: [your store address]' as literal text. public/index.html:7 still describes 'A product of emergent.sh' and :24 sets title 'Emergent | Fullstack App'; no app component updates document.title or supplies a real support destination.
findings_minor.expected: request: "everything should be clear"; checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: "product-specific branding/content" and visible action outcomes; users rely on: the explicitly displayed Support contact being usable. Shoppers should see MiniBasket identity and a real support contact for order/payment problems.
reproduction_steps: Open any storefront page and inspect its browser title.
Scroll to Company in the footer.
Support and store address are bracketed placeholders with no usable contact.
